researcher_notes: Son My is a multi-phase project: Phase 1 = 3.6 MTPA, Phase 2 = 6 MTPA. The 6 MTPA Phase 2 was explicitly enumerated when the project received Binh Thuan investment-policy approval on 11 Jul 2023 (both verified sources are 2023). LOW-CONFIDENCE / milestone caveat: the multi-phase concept (3.6/6/10 MTPA) dates to PV Gas's 2015 feasibility study and the project's ~Oct 2019 government approval, so the true 'first publicly proposed' year of the Phase 2 expansion may be ~2015-2019. 2023 is the verifiable point at which Phase 2 = 6 MTPA was formally defined in the sanctioned project; reviewer should confirm whether GEM's Phase 2 'proposed' milestone is the original-plan year or the 2023 sanction. Web-search budget (session limit) was exhausted before an earlier year could be independently verified.

Thi Vai Phase 2 = expansion of the existing 1 MTPA terminal to 3 MTPA. Petrovietnam formally directed PV Gas to triple capacity to 3 MTPA at a 3 Feb 2025 working session, with PV Gas ready to sign the EPC contract in late 2025 (both verified sources are Feb 2025, independent publishers). LOW-CONFIDENCE / milestone caveat: the 3 MTPA second phase already appeared in the project's original phased design (Phase 1 = 1 MTPA ops ~2023, Phase 2 = 3 MTPA), so the 'first publicly proposed' year may be ~2019-2021. 2025 is the verifiable formal expansion proposal; reviewer should confirm whether GEM's Phase 2 'proposed' milestone is the original-plan year or the 2025 directive. Web-search budget (session limit) was exhausted before an earlier year could be independently verified.

The Tien Lang FSRU was part of ExxonMobil's ~$5.09bn Tien Lang 1 IP LNG-to-power complex (Haiphong 1, 4,500 MW). Cancellation is GEM-inferred (substatus 'inferred 4 y'). Best-documented abandonment event: the Tien Lang / Haiphong LNG-power projects were dropped from the draft Power Development Plan 8 submitted 21 Feb 2022 (verified source, The Investor, 19 Mar 2022). The project was not in final PDP8 (approved May 2023); offshore-technology (Oct 2021) still listed it as merely proposed, and there is no later activity. Staged 2022 = year removed from the national power plan = de facto cancellation. Single independent media source (no primary/regulatory filing accessible), hence tier low; the 2022 value itself is well-supported.

No independent source gives a specific YEAR that Bontang/Badak Train A was retired/decommissioned. Sources only describe aggregate decline: IGU 2020 World LNG Report reported trains A & B no longer operating; GIIGNL 2021 reported ~4 trains running; Jakarta Post (Jul 2021) reported only 2 trains operating; Indonesian reactivation coverage (Train F target Oct 2028) explicitly states no per-train shutdown years and that A/B/C are 'no longer active, service life exhausted.' No page ties Train A to a dated retirement event. Web-search budget (session limit) exhausted. UNRESOLVED.

No independent source gives a specific YEAR that Bontang/Badak Train B was retired/decommissioned. Same evidentiary gap as Train A: IGU 2020 World LNG Report noted trains A & B no longer operating, but sources lump A/B/C/D together without dated per-train shutdowns; Indonesian reactivation articles confirm no specific years are published. Web-search budget exhausted. UNRESOLVED.

No independent source gives a specific YEAR that Bontang/Badak Train C was retired/decommissioned. Sources describe C/D as 'preparing for decommissioning' (circa 2020-2021) and, more recently, A/B/C as 'no longer active,' but with no dated retirement event for Train C. Aggregate decline only. Web-search budget exhausted. UNRESOLVED.

No independent source gives a specific YEAR that Bontang/Badak Train D was retired/decommissioned. Train D is variously described as 'long-term idle' and 'preparing for decommissioning' (circa 2020-2021); no dated retirement event is published. Aggregate decline only. Web-search budget exhausted. UNRESOLVED.

No independent source gives a specific YEAR that Bontang/Badak Train E was idled. Train E is described as 'idle/standby (reserve)' in recent (2024-2026) Indonesian coverage, but no source dates the transition to idle. By 2023-2024 only trains G & H were operating, implying E was idled earlier, but no dated event is published. Web-search budget exhausted. UNRESOLVED.

No independent source gives a specific YEAR that Bontang/Badak Train F was idled. Train F is the subject of a 2024-2026 reactivation plan (first LNG targeted Oct 2027/2028) following the Geng North-1 gas discovery (2023), which confirms F is currently idle, but no source dates when Train F stopped operating. Indonesian articles explicitly state no per-train shutdown years are available. Web-search budget exhausted. UNRESOLVED.

Cancellation is GEM-inferred (substatus 'inferred 4 y'). The terminal (Panbil Group / PT Nusatama Properta Panbil, on Pulau Asam, Karimun) had a USTDA feasibility-study grant awarded in July 2020 (NS Energy, 19 Aug 2020) as its last documented activity, with no progress reported since. No independent source states a cancellation/abandonment year; the inferred year (~2024 = 2020 last activity + 4y) is not citable. Web-search budget exhausted. UNRESOLVED for a sourced cancellation year.

EWC's Sengkang LNG (South Sulawesi). Work on the near-complete Train 1 was halted/suspended in 2017 amid forestry-permit / land disputes (resolved 2020). Primary corroboration: the Energy World Corporation ASX announcement (29 Aug 2025), a sponsor regulatory filing, references 2017 alongside Sengkang (verified). CAVEAT: EWC announced a revival in 2021 and completed the sale of its 51% Sengkang interest in Oct 2024 (2024 also present in the same ASX filing) — so the project's current 'shelved' state could alternatively date to the post-2024 dormancy. Staged 2017 as the documented suspension year (matches the 'shelved' milestone at timeline_order 3). Tier medium: single primary source (energyvoice.com second source returned HTTP 403; petromindo article is login-walled, no '2017' in fetchable body).

Sengkang LNG T2-T4 expansion. The same 2017 work-halt/suspension applied to the whole Sengkang project (Train 1 plus the planned T2-T4 expansion) amid forestry-permit / land disputes (resolved 2020). Primary corroboration: EWC ASX announcement (29 Aug 2025) references 2017 alongside Sengkang (verified). CAVEAT: project revived 2021; EWC divested its 51% interest Oct 2024 (2024 also in the filing), so an alternative reading places the current shelving post-2024. Staged 2017 as the documented suspension year (timeline_order 3). Tier medium: single primary source available.
